papers.title: Surface and Biocompatibility Outcomes of Chemical Decontamination in Peri-Implantitis Management
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: Peri-implantitis is a biologically driven complication that jeopardizes dental implant longevity. While chemical decontamination is frequently employed as an adjunct to mechanical debridement, its impact on implant surface integrity and cellular compatibility remains insufficiently defined. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of several chemical agents used in peri-implantitis treatment on the surface morphology and potential biocompatibility of titanium dental implants. Materials and Methods: Twenty-five Ti6Al4V implants were exposed to one of the following agents: saline solution, 3% hydrogen peroxide, 40% citric acid, 17% EDTA, and a mixture (1:1) of citric (2%) and phosphoric (1N) acids. This in vitro study employed a 7-day immersion protocol to accentuate surface effects under controlled laboratory conditions, acknowledging that clinical exposures are substantially shorter. Surface topography was evaluated by Atomic Force Microscopy, while cellular response and corrosion products were assessed using Scanning Electron Microscopy. Surface roughness parameters were statistically analyzed. Results: Hydrogen peroxide induced selective corrosion of the β phase and formed a compact passivation layer that supported mesenchymal stem cell adhesion. Citric acid etched grain boundaries, producing localized roughness that also permitted cell proliferation. EDTA caused advanced grain dissolution and debris accumulation, increasing surface roughness but impairing cellular adhesion. The citric–phosphoric acid mixture led to the highest roughness values and visible corrosion debris. In all cases, macrostructural integrity of the implants was preserved. Conclusions: Chemical agents used in peri-implantitis treatment induce distinct surface alterations on titanium implants. Controlled use of hydrogen peroxide and citric acid may enhance surface biocompatibility, while aggressive protocols such as EDTA and acid combinations require caution due to their adverse effects on surface morphology and cellular response. These findings may inform the development of optimized decontamination protocols for clinical management of peri-implantitis.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文虽涉及Ti-6Al-4V和化学处理，但聚焦于牙周炎消毒而非力学性能改进。
llm.why_not_core: No evaluation of mechanical performance (fatigue, tensile) or porosity closure; the study is about biocompatibility for dental implant decontamination, not post-processing for improved mechanical properties.

summary_zh.motivation: 探讨化学去污剂对牙种植体表面和生物相容性的影响，为牙周炎治疗提供依据。
summary_zh.method: 将Ti6Al4V植入体浸泡于不同化学试剂中7天，使用AFM和SEM评估表面形貌和细胞响应。
summary_zh.result: 过氧化氢和柠檬酸可改善表面生物相容性，而EDTA和酸混合物增加粗糙度但损害细胞黏附。
summary_zh.validation: 体外实验通过材料表征和细胞培养验证表面变化和生物相容性。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the effects of chemical agents used in peri-implantitis treatment on titanium implant surface integrity and biocompatibility.
summary_en.method: Ti6Al4V dental implants were immersed in saline, hydrogen peroxide, citric acid, EDTA, or a citric-phosphoric acid mixture for 7 days, followed by AFM and SEM analysis of surface morphology and cell adhesion.
summary_en.result: Hydrogen peroxide and citric acid promoted favorable surface characteristics and cell adhesion, while EDTA and acid mixtures increased roughness and compromised biocompatibility.
summary_en.validation: In vitro experiments with surface characterization and mesenchymal stem cell culture validated the chemical-induced surface changes and cellular responses.

papers.title: Artificial Joints in Prosthetic Limbs Enhancing Materials for Durability and Biocompatibility
papers.abstract: The number of people who lose a limb is over 1 million every year throughout the world and is most commonly due to an accident, disease, or from birth. Current prosthetic development focuses on the mobility aspect, with little attention given to the material used in the artificial joint, which must be successful over the long term for the overall success of the prosthetic limb. The metals traditionally employed in prosthetics are Cobalt-Chromium-Molybdenum (Co-Cr-Mo) and Titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V), polymers are Ultra-High Molecular Weight Polyethylene (UHMWPE) and Polyether Ether Ketone (PEEK), and ceramics are Alumina <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(\text{Al}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}\right)$</tex> and Zirconia <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(\text{ZrO}_{2}\right)$</tex>. Five composite samples offering varied proportions of constituent materials were fabricated and tested in this research. Statistical validation using one-way ANOVA and p-values (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p<0.05$</tex>) confirmed that the observed differences among samples were significant. Sample A (60% metal, 30% ceramic, 10% polymer) exhibited the highest hardness (96 HV) and tensile strength (195 MPa) with lower cytocompatibility (85%). Sample E (20% metal, 60% ceramic, 20% polymer) showed the highest cell viability and adhesion (96% and 92%, respectively) but lower tensile strength (150 MPa). Sample C (40% metal, 40% ceramic, 20% polymer) had the best overall performance: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$88 \text{HV}, 176 \text{MPa}$</tex>, bioactivity index of 99, and 91% viable cells. Results confirmed that material balance is the core factor in improving both structural integrity and biological response. While accelerated fatigue, cyclic loading, and long-term wear tests under simulated joint conditions remain a limitation of this study, they are recommended for future validation. Findings indicate that composite design should be customized to specific prosthetic requirements. This study forms a critical input in the development of advanced load-bearing artificial joints with enhanced performance and reduced rejection risk.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究的是用于假肢关节的复合材料，并非增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的力学或疲劳性能。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not focus on additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V; it studies composite materials (metal/ceramic/polymer) for prosthetic joints without any AM context, fatigue testing, or Ti-6Al-4V-specific mechanical characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 假肢关节材料对长期成功至关重要，但目前关注不足。
summary_zh.method: 制备五种不同比例的金属-陶瓷-聚合物复合材料并测试其力学与生物学性能。
summary_zh.result: 样品C（40%金属、40%陶瓷、20%聚合物）综合性能最佳。
summary_zh.validation: 通过单因素方差分析统计验证样品间差异显著。

summary_en.motivation: The long-term success of prosthetic limbs depends on the material choice for artificial joints, which has received insufficient attention.
summary_en.method: Five composite samples with varying proportions of metal, ceramic, and polymer were fabricated and tested for hardness, tensile strength, and cytocompatibility.
summary_en.result: Sample C (40% metal, 40% ceramic, 20% polymer) exhibited the best overall performance with balanced mechanical and biological properties.
summary_en.validation: One-way ANOVA confirmed statistically significant differences among the samples (p<0.05).
